text:
sara_support: FYI escalated from ACME Retail — multiple API calls from their on-prem app are hitting our APAC egress and showing ~250-400ms extra latency. Customer insists they’re US-based and pinned to us-west. Repro steps and prints below.

sara_support: Repro (from their NAT appliance):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' -i
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Region: apac-sg1
X-Request-ID: rwd-req-6321
X-Forwarded-For: 54.12.34.56
```

sara_support: traceroute from their edge (anonymized):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.200.1.1)
 1  10.1.0.1  0.6 ms
 2  198.51.100.2  1.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.5 (apac-hub)  120.3 ms
 4  34.200.1.1  121.1 ms
```

sara_support: They also included a NAT debug snippet from their edge showing SNAT to our peered hub IP: `203.0.113.5`.

sara_support: Ticket: INC-98123. Customer requests we stop APAC egress for their VPC until we’re sure. Asking for quick mitigation + root cause. :exclamation:

mike_net: Thanks — adding network oncall. Two quick asks: can you paste the VPC id + TGW attachment id and route table that the customer is using? suspect TGW route propagation or an AS path/local-pref difference favouring apac-hub. Also: are they using AWS Transit Gateway route table propagation or static routes?

sara_support: VPC: vpc-0abc1234, TGW-att: tgw-attach-0f2, they said route table is using propagated routes. I'll add the flow logs they provided.

alex_runtime: Noted. From the runtime side: we tag backend choices by X-Region header and by nearest replica via smart routing; fallback logic picks a compatible variant if local capacity isn't available. However this customer shows X-Redwood-Region coming back as apac-sg1 — that means our front-door selected APAC as the egress for that request. Can we confirm whether their egress IP is being translated by the hub to an APAC public IP?

nate_oncall: Quick network checks I ran on the peering config:
```
# tgw routes (shortened)
0.0.0.0/0 -> local-igw
10.0.0.0/8 -> propagate (via attachments: usw-hub, apac-hub)
# BGP adverts show apac-hub AS path shorter for 10.1.0.0/24 due to missing prepends
```
nate_oncall: Looks like apac-hub is advertising the customer's onprem prefix with higher local-pref (or shorter AS path) — causes return traffic to prefer APAC hub. Also saw NAT rule on hub that SNATs to 203.0.113.5 which is APAC egress IP.

mike_net: That matches. Two likely causes: 1) route propagation duplicated in multiple TGW route tables with different priorities, or 2) onprem->TGW path prefers apac due to BGP attributes. Immediate mitigation options: a) set explicit static route in their TGW route table pointing to us-west attachment for the affected prefix, or b) apply an egress override on our side for that customer to prefer us-west (short-term).

alex_runtime: We can inject a per-customer region override in the routing policy: add header X-Force-Region: us-west to keep the request local while you fix infra. I can push a small config change for a targeted customer label (will be a routing config update, no deploy). Need ticket + customer org id.

julia_success: I'll update INC-98123 with the suggested workaround (X-Force-Region) and ask for customer's permission to test it. Also: are there logging traces we should capture to prove reroute? request-id listed above (rwd-req-6321).

sara_support: Customer okay with temporary override; gave org ID acme-retail-22. Please proceed.

alex_runtime: Done — pushed routing override for acme-retail-22 -> us-west. Confirming now:
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"X-Force-Region: us-west\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping -I
< X-Redwood-Region: us-west-1
```
alex_runtime: Can someone ask customer to validate latency is back to expected (~30-50ms)?

sara_support: They validated: latency dropped to ~40ms, confirmed no APAC egress observed. Thanks.

mike_net: For long-term fix we should: 1) have customer remove ambiguous route propagation and create explicit route preference in TGW (propagate only from us-west attachment), 2) adjust BGP advertisements from their onprem so apac-hub doesn't become preferred (AS path prepend or lower local-pref), OR 3) pin that VPC to a single hub via TGW route table scoping. I'll open a network action ticket with required route config diffs.

nate_oncall: I'll also add an alert to our peering-monitor: detect when a customer's public source IP maps to a nonpreferred region hub (based on mapping table), and trigger a warning if traffic suddenly flips region for >5% of requests in 10m.

julia_success: I'll follow up with ACME CSM to coordinate the TGW/Terraform changes and capture remediation steps for our runbook.

deploy-bot: Started runbook update job #rb-402: adding section \"private-egress: region misroute triage\" — link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rb-402

sara_support: closing loop in ticket: temporary override applied and validated, long-term network changes in flight. Keeping this thread for notes. :white_check_mark:
